summary: 42 U.S.C. §1983 (Monell & Individual Capacity), Bane Act (Cal. Civ. Code §52.1), Fraud / Negligent Misrepresentation, RICO (18 U.S.C. §1962(c)-(d)), UCL (Bus. & Prof. Code §17200), Negligence Per Se

counts.title: Count 1 — 42 U.S.C. §1983 (Monell / Institutional Liability against CPC): delegation of public function under West v. Atkins; unconstitutional policy, custom, or practice of indefinite containment-model retention

Count 2 — 42 U.S.C. §1983 (Individual Capacity against Executive / Clinical Officers): supervisory and individual liability for unconstitutional retention directives, retaliatory adverse reporting, and due process deprivations
Count 3 — Tom Bane Civil Rights Act, Cal. Civ. Code §52.1: coercive interference with constitutional and statutory rights under Pen. Code §3008(d)(2) and 15 CCR §3574(f)(1)
Count 4 — Fraud and Intentional / Negligent Misrepresentation: intake representations of individualized clinical graduation criteria vs. concealed blanket retention policies
Count 5 — Negligence and Negligence Per Se: duty of care under Giraldo; violation of mandatory statutory and regulatory standards governing sex offender treatment completion
Count 6 — Intentional Interference with Prospective Economic Advantage: disruption of Class A CDL commercial driving employment and refusal of reasonable scheduling accommodations
Count 7 — Unfair Competition Law, Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §17200: unlawful and unfair business practices regarding fee-for-service client billing and retention models; restitution of client-paid fees
Count 8 — Declaratory and Injunctive Relief: judicial declaration that blanket non-completion policies violate California law; permanent injunction requiring individualized CASOMB assessment
